deviations: [5] wording: I followed the refuter's design (count reserved rows a refusal set aside, say they stand for nothing, and tell the validator) but used neutral words. The message says 'its number was refused before the row was read', not 'a newer section had refused its number'. Reason: the count includes a row the stream's own earlier row for the same number refused, and for that row 'a newer section' would be false. The read-in-part reports keep 'a newer section' for other sections' refusals only.

[4]: I took the refuter's first option, keeping the refusing section with each number. _refusedNumbers is now Dictionary<int, XRefSectionRecord> instead of a per-section set. It is still allocated only on the first refusal, so a valid file allocates nothing.

[15] goes slightly beyond the refuter's text. KeptButFor is also used in ReportLostSection, the 'cannot be read' arm, where a table that refused its own row before a fatal fault said 'the rows read before the fault, if any, were kept'. Same falsehood; one test covers it.

[9] design follows the refuter (the keyword's line lexed as HeaderText lexes a line, bounded and allocation-free) with two refinements. First, it reads up to two tokens past the keyword's line outside comments rather than one line, because a generation and obj may sit on separate lines such as '12 % endstream\n0 % c\nobj'. Second, it tests only that one obj with HeaderText.HeaderAt rather than calling FindHeader up to it, so a fake header inside a later comment cannot mask the real one. A search that can read no further takes the keyword, as the first endstream always ended the data before: past the budget, at an empty source, or a parser alone given a window that leaves it undecided for a larger one.

[9] property: the refuter's suggested property ('the data ends at the same place whether the index places the header's object or not') is checked at document level inside the WindowEdge theory, at two fillers. The FsCheck property added instead holds split independence of the search with the waiting keyword.

open_points: Docs stage, docs/website/docs/concepts/diagnostics.md:42-55 (and the 'whichever comes first' at :43-46): add that an endstream which a comment between a header's tokens holds ends no data before that header. Such an endstream, first in the data, inside a comment on a line whose tokens may begin a header, waits for the first token past its line outside a comment (or two, where the first is a run of digits). It ends the data only when no header that starts before it ends there. A search that can read no further takes it.
